messages:
mike: FYI we started seeing a spike in GPU host crashes after the kernel batch upgrade to 6.1.x in eu-west yesterday. node status shows OOM/oom_kill and 'nvidia' kmod failing to load on some nodes

tara: ugh. same here in staging — pods stuck Pending with ImagePullBackOff? or actually CrashLoopBackOff on gpu-drivers-daemonset. logs show module init failures.

kevin: can you paste the modprobe logs? I suspect mismatched ABI between kernel and prebuilt nvidia module (we've been shipping prebuilt .run installer artifacts pinned to kernel-abi for 5.15)

mike: log snippet: 
```
Jul 12 03:12:01 host kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol module_layout
Jul 12 03:12:01 host kernel: nvidia: Unknown symbol nvidia_pci_register_driver (err -22)
Jul 12 03:12:01 host kernel: kernel: nvidia: disagrees about version of symbol do_gettimeofday64
```

sarah: ^ classic kmod ABI mismatch. Also saw "tainted: P" in dmesg which matches third-party module load failure.

tara: staging hosts were on kernel 6.1.0-rcX, prod got 6.0.11 -> several host reboots happened and kubelet marked nodes NotReady after driver pod failed to mount /dev/nvidia*

oncall-james: we rolled back the kernel to 5.15 on 3 nodes as emergency rollback earlier to recover capacity. That freed up 12 GPUs for critical tenant jobs.

kevin: long-term fix options: 1) rebuild nvidia driver DKMS modules against 6.x kernels and publish artifacts per kernel-abi; 2) pin node groups to kernel major versions and schedule upgrade waves while draining GPUs; 3) ship kernel-compat shim or use in-tree module packaging.

mike: rebuilding drivers affects CUDA/runtime pairings too — some older CUDA 11.X runtimes fail against driver built with new gcc ABI. Need CI to build driver + cuda-runtime combos for kernel matrix.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1453 "gpu-host-driver-failures-after-kernel-6x". Pager notified.

tara: can we gate kernel upgrades on a successful canary where the driver daemonset loads OK and a quick cuda-sanity pod runs? That would have caught this.

kevin: agreed. propose: (A) disable autopush for linux-image on gpu nodegroups, (B) create canary pool of 5 nodes per region to validate driver install + nvml smoke test, (C) add DKMS build job in infra-ci to publish kernel-specific nvidia module packages, (D) add rollback playbook to ops-runbook.

sarah: also note cost/availability impact — when we rollback/cordon GPU nodes we lose capacity and shift pods to other regions. We hit quota and started bursting to on-demand which increased spend ~18% yesterday. Need to include cost estimate in rollout docs.

mike: created a short checklist in PR #2843 with the canary gating and cost calc. Link: https://git.redwood/infrateam/pr/2843 (internal)

oncall-james: immediate next steps: pin kernel package on remaining upgrade wave, schedule DKMS rebuild for 6.1 and 6.0 series, run canary tomorrow 02:00 UTC, notify tenants about possible GPU evictions. I'll own the rollback playbook.

tara: I'll add smoke tests: nvcc --version, nvidia-smi, run simple tensor concat test, and an nvjpeg pipeline to catch runtime-level breakages.

kevin: one more gotcha — NCCL/libcudnn ABI sometimes needs driver minor version; we should include model-serving smoke (bert small inference) to validate latency and correctness.

mike: thanks all. add @security to the thread — kernel taints could affect compliance. Also add a note to the Release Engineering channel before resuming upgrades. :eyes:

sarah: pinged release-eng and security. I'll prepare the cost impact report and a quick postmortem template to attach to the incident.

infra-bot: Update: INC-2026-1453 status -> mitigated (drivers pinned, canary scheduled).
